lines.japanese: 「よし、たまには高内さんと一緒に帰るか」
lines.english: “All right. I suppose I can walk home with you for once, Takauchi.”

lines.japanese: 「あん？　つか、ナンダソノたまにはって。なんで羽田、そんな上から目線なん？」
lines.english: “Huh? The hell's that ‘for once’ supposed to mean? Why're you talking down to me, Haneda?”

lines.japanese: 「ん、偉そうだったか？　それは悪かった、言いなおそう。さあ高内さん一緒に薔薇色の下校をしよう！」
lines.english: “Hm? Did that sound condescending? My apologies. Let me try again. Come, Takauchi! Let us share a rose-colored walk home!”

lines.japanese: 「おっ、いいね羽田。よーし、途中のコンビニでなんか買って食いながら歩こうぜ」
lines.english: “Ooh, now you're talking. All right, let's grab something at the convenience store and eat while we walk.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、それならちょうどよかった。俺、ちょっと服かえたいからさ、コンビニのトイレで着替えていいかな」
lines.english: “Oh, perfect. I need to change clothes, so can I use the convenience-store bathroom?”

lines.japanese: 「服？　なんで？」
lines.english: “Change? Why?”

lines.japanese: 「アルバイト先で学生だってバレると給料下がるから」
lines.english: “If they find out I'm a student at work, they'll cut my pay.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、なるほどね。はー、確かに他のフリーター連中よっか時給低いとアホらしーわ。かー、羽田やっぱ頭いいな」
lines.english: “Oh, yeah, makes sense. Getting paid less than all the other part-timers would be bullshit. Damn, Haneda, you really are smart.”

lines.japanese: 「だからアルバイト先で見かけても、学生だってことはナイショにしといてね！」
lines.english: “So if you see me at work, keep it a secret that I'm a student!”

lines.japanese: 「おっけおっけ。任せとけって」
lines.english: “Sure, sure. Leave it to me.”

lines.japanese: よし、これでアレキサンダーへ行く前に着替えられるぞ。よかったよかった。
lines.english: Good. Now I could change before going to Alexander. Excellent.

lines.japanese: 「へー、羽田のアルバイト先ってここなん」
lines.english: “Huh. So this is where you work, Haneda.”

lines.japanese: 二本目の唐揚げ串を頬張りながら、高内昌子はアレキサンダーの煙突を見上げていた。
lines.english: Masako Takauchi looked up at Alexander's chimney as she bit into her second fried-chicken skewer.

lines.japanese: おかしいな、だらだら話しつつ適当な場所で別れるつもりだったのに、どうして俺のアルバイト先にまで連れてきてしまったんだろう。
lines.english: How strange. I had meant to ramble for a while and part ways somewhere convenient. How had I ended up bringing her all the way to my workplace?

lines.japanese: 「私も何回か来たことあんよ。つかよく今まで会わなかったよね」
lines.english: “I've been here a few times. Kinda amazing we never ran into each other.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、俺がここで働きはじめて、まだ一ヶ月ちょいだからな」
lines.english: “Well, I only started working here a little over a month ago.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、そーなん。なに？　やっぱ制服目当て？　人気あるよなー、ここの制服。なんかうちのクラスの男でも、大したモン頼むわけでもねーのに、よくウェイトレス目当てで来てるやついるんだって」
lines.english: “Oh, yeah? What, were you after the uniforms? They're popular. I hear some guys in our class come here for the waitresses even when they don't want much.”

lines.japanese: 「つか私も髪の色さえなければ、面接受けてもよかったんだけどー」
lines.english: “I might've applied myself if it weren't for my hair color.”

lines.japanese: ははは、高内昌子は流石だなあ。雇われることに対して、使ってもらう側という意識が微塵もない。
lines.english: Hahaha. That was Masako Takauchi for you. Not for an instant did she think of herself as the one asking to be hired.

lines.japanese: 「なに羽田、やっぱ制服とか好きなん」
lines.english: “What, Haneda, you into uniforms?”

lines.japanese: 「制服……うん、嫌いじゃないと言えば嘘になるが、どっちかと言えば素材そのものを生かした学校指定のジャージとかの方が……」
lines.english: “Uniforms... I'd be lying if I said I disliked them, but personally, I prefer school-issued tracksuits that let the raw material speak for itself...”

lines.japanese: 「は？　ジャージ？　なにそれ、それが萌えってやつなん？」
lines.english: “What? Tracksuits? Is that one of those things that melts your heart?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いや萌えっていうか、個人的な趣味嗜好というか。あ、俺、シスコンとかロリコンとか考えたこともないけどね」
lines.english: “N-no, less heart-melting than a matter of personal taste. Oh, and I’ve never had a sister complex or a Lolita complex.”

lines.japanese: 「シスコン？　つかロリコンとかきもくね？　きめっ、あいつらチョーきめえ」
lines.english: “Sister complex? Wait, aren’t guys with a Lolita complex fucking gross? God, those creeps are seriously disgusting.”

lines.japanese: 「気持ち悪くなどない！」
lines.english: “They are not disgusting!”

lines.japanese: 「俺、ロリコンとか全然ないけどね！」
lines.english: “Not that I have a Lolita complex or anything!”

lines.japanese: 「あ、つーかさ、ちょっと聞きたいことあんだけど」
lines.english: “Oh, hey. There's something I wanna ask you.”

lines.japanese: 「ん、質問か？　ここじゃ寒いから、どうせ話すなら店の中へ入ろう」
lines.english: “A question? It's cold out here, so if we're going to talk, let's go inside.”

lines.japanese: 「だな。そーすっか」
lines.english: “Yeah. Sounds good.”

lines.japanese: 気がつけば俺は、高内昌子とアレキサンダーの中へ入っていた。
lines.english: Before I knew it, Masako Takauchi and I had entered Alexander.

lines.japanese: 「いらっしゃいませ、お二人様で――」
lines.english: “Welcome. A table for two—”

lines.japanese: 「――おっ、鷲介！　今日もまた学生服姿の女の子を連れて、羨ましいぞう！」
lines.english: “—oh, Shuusuke! Another girl in a school uniform today? You lucky dog!”

lines.japanese: 「あン？　シュースケ？」
lines.english: “Huh? Shuusuke?”

lines.japanese: 「い、いや、あだ名なんだ、ははは。そ、それよりマスター！　非番なのに遊びに来ちゃってすみません！」
lines.english: “I-it's a nickname! Hahaha. M-more importantly, Boss! Sorry I dropped in on my day off!”

lines.japanese: 「構わん構わん。見ろ、この時間帯。客は少ないし店員は足りてる」
lines.english: “Not at all. Look around. Few customers and plenty of staff at this hour.”

lines.japanese: 「おまえがいても働き手を余らすだけだ。それよりも客として来てもらった方が、こっちも大助かりだ」
lines.english: “If you were here, I'd only have an extra worker on my hands. You're far more helpful as a customer.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ、そう言ってもらえるとこちらも……あ、そういえば玉泉教官は？」
lines.english: “Well, if you put it that way... Oh, right. Where's Instructor Tamaizumi?”

lines.japanese: 「玉泉君？　玉泉君なら今日は元々シフトに入ってないぞ」
lines.english: “Tamaizumi? She wasn't scheduled today in the first place.”

lines.japanese: 「げっ！」
lines.english: “Gah!”

lines.japanese: な、なんだよ、玉泉のひと休みかよ。それじゃ今日中にチケットの交渉をするのは無理じゃないか。
lines.english: W-what the hell? Tamaizumi had the day off? Then there was no way I could ask her about the ticket today.

lines.japanese: 困ったな、それじゃあ明日の当日券に期待するしかない……。
lines.english: This was a problem. All I could do now was hope for tickets at the door tomorrow...

lines.japanese: 「おいおい、女性の連れがいるときに他の女の話をするとはどういうつもりだ」
lines.english: “Now, now. What kind of man talks about another woman while he has a lady with him?”

lines.japanese: なんて考えていたら、マスターに駄目出しをされてしまった。
lines.english: As I pondered my predicament, the boss called me out.

lines.japanese: 「ひとのことより、まず自分の連れてきた女性をエスコートしろ。男が女を待たせていいのは、ベッドの上で達するときだけだぜ」
lines.english: “Forget everyone else and escort the woman you brought. The only time a man should keep a woman waiting is when he's about to come in bed.”

lines.japanese: 「ハードボイルド風になにか言いたかったんでしょうけど、なりきれてませんね」
lines.english: “You were trying to sound hard-boiled, but you didn't quite get there.”

lines.japanese: 「ふん、禁煙席でいいな？」
lines.english: “Hmph. Nonsmoking, I assume?”

lines.japanese: 「まあ玉泉が居ないなら適当にだべって帰るか……よし行こう、高内さん」
lines.english: “Well, if Tamaizumi isn't here, we may as well shoot the breeze and go home... Come on, Takauchi.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ」
lines.english: “Right.”

lines.japanese: 「ではごゆっくり。夜は長いからな、くくく」
lines.english: “Enjoy yourselves. The night is long. Heh heh heh.”

lines.japanese: 「悪い。あのひと、知り合いには下ギャグを一つ挟まないと気が済まないタイプなんだ」
lines.english: “Sorry. He's the type who can't talk to an acquaintance without slipping in at least one dirty joke.”

lines.japanese: 「はー。ま、いーけど。うちらも似たようなもんだし」
lines.english: “Huh. Whatever. We're pretty much the same.”

lines.japanese: 「ははは、高内さんたちは一つ挟むどころか、下ネタの中にまっとうな単語が一つだけある感じだよね。おっとそういえば、なにか聞きたいことがあるとか言ってなかったか」
lines.english: “Hahaha. You girls don't slip one dirty joke into a conversation so much as slip one decent word into a stream of filth. Oh, right. Didn't you say you had something to ask me?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そーそー。誰に聞いても分かんないから羽田に聞くわ。あのさ、萌えってなんなん？」
lines.english: “Oh, yeah. Nobody else knows, so I’ll ask you. What’s this whole ‘melts your heart’ thing?”

lines.japanese: 「ん、萌えか」
lines.english: “Heart-melting appeal, huh?”

lines.japanese: この前も同じ質問されたな。高内昌子はそんなに萌え文化に興味があるのか。
lines.english: Someone had asked me that same question recently. Was Masako Takauchi really so interested in the culture of heart-melting characters?

lines.japanese: まあ個人的な差があるのは否めないとして……。
lines.english: Admittedly, personal tastes varied...

lines.japanese: 「外見的な特徴で言えば、髪は黒、着てる服はジャージ……な感じで、性格で言えば素朴で優しい……感じで、名前で言えばカ行とバ行とタ行が入ってる……感じで、存在感で言えば女神な感じかな」
lines.english: “In terms of appearance, black hair and a tracksuit... In terms of personality, simple and kind... In terms of her name, the letters K, B, and T... And in terms of presence, a goddess.”

lines.japanese: 「んだそれ、注文多いな。もっと絞れよ」
lines.english: “What the hell? That's way too many conditions. Narrow it down.”

lines.japanese: 「ばっ、なにを言ってるんだ、注文なんて付けてない！　俺はただ、ありのままの小ばっ……萌えについて説明しただけだ！」
lines.english: “Wh-what are you talking about? Those aren’t conditions! I merely described Koba—heart-melting appeal exactly as it is!”

lines.japanese: 「まあ萌えについてというか、萌えの象徴的な存在が一人いるからな。具体例を挙げてみただけだ」
lines.english: “More to the point, there is one person who embodies heart-melting appeal. I simply offered a concrete example.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、そーなん？　つか誰よ。どんなんよ。やっぱ渡来みたいな？　それとも山科みたいなん？」
lines.english: “Oh, yeah? Who? What's she like? Someone like Watarai? Or Yamashina?”

lines.japanese: 「アホぬかせ、渡来明日香なんかとは比べるべくもない。この世の美しさを全て凝縮したような、雪か天使かエーデルワイスかというくらいの純白さだ。彼女ほどの萌えキャラは、今世紀中にはまず出まい」
lines.english: “Don’t be absurd. She is beyond comparison with Asuka Watarai. All the beauty in the world seems distilled into her, pure white as snow, an angel, or edelweiss. This century will never produce another character with such heart-melting appeal.”

lines.japanese: 「はー。そんじゃ、やっぱ羽田はそーゆーのがいいんだ。で、純白ってどんなん？」
lines.english: “Huh. So that's your type, Haneda. What's this ‘pure white’ girl like?”

lines.japanese: 「いやよく考えたら、俺、シスコンとかロリコンとか全然ないから分からないや」
lines.english: “Come to think of it, I've never had a sister complex or a Lolita complex, so I wouldn't know.”

lines.japanese: 「なんで。いま自分からべらべらしゃべってたじゃん。もっと特徴とか教えてよ」
lines.english: “What? You just volunteered that whole damn speech. Tell me more about her.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ、それは構わないが、どうしたんだ高内さん。萌えキャラにでもなろうとしてるのか」
lines.english: “I don’t mind, but what’s gotten into you, Takauchi? Are you trying to become the heart-melting type?”

lines.japanese: 「はあ？　私が萌えキャラ？　ぶはっ、んだそれマジ受ける。つかそーじゃねーよ。ちっと話題になってっから、キャラ抑えとこーと思っただけだよ」
lines.english: “What? Me, the heart-melting type? Pfft! That’s fucking hilarious. Nah. People have been talking about it, so I just wanted to get a handle on the archetype.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、なるほどなあ。でもキャラ抑えるだけなら、記号的な部分だけ抑えておけばいいと思うぞ。言動とか外見とか調べたら山ほど出てくるしな」
lines.english: “Oh, I see. If all you need is the archetype, you can focus on the symbolic traits. You'll find mountains of examples if you look up their behavior and appearance.”

lines.japanese: 「外見ってなによ。やっぱ白パンツとか？」
lines.english: “What kind of appearance? White panties?”

lines.japanese: 「その言動からまずアウトだな。つうか今の時代なら白よりも縞パ――」
lines.english: “That line alone disqualifies you. Besides, these days stripes are more popular than wh—”

lines.japanese: 「――ん？　そこの子供なにしてるんだ？」
lines.english: “—hm? What's that child doing?”

lines.japanese: 「あン？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「おねーえちゃんっ」
lines.english: “Big sisteeer!”

lines.japanese: 「なんだこのクソガキ。つかいま会議中だから、どっかいけ」
lines.english: “What do you want, brat? We're in the middle of a meeting, so get lost.”

lines.japanese: 「おねーちゃん、しましまでしょ」
lines.english: “Big sister, yours are striped, right?”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　しつっけーなガキ、誰でも甘やかすと思ってんじゃねーぞ。親どこだ親」
lines.english: “What? Persistent little brat. Don't think everybody's gonna spoil you. Where are your parents?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、席立った！」
lines.english: “Oh, she stood up!”

lines.japanese: 「はあ？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「わーい、おねーえちゃんっ！」
lines.english: “Yay, big sisteeer!”

lines.japanese: 「ぎゃあああーっ！」
lines.english: “GYAAAAH!”

lines.japanese: 「♪しましまだあ～、しっましまだあ～」
lines.english: “♪ They're striiiped! Stripy-striiiped!”

lines.japanese: 「なっ、なにしてんだこのガキ、ちょちょちょいまはやめろ、つか離せって！」
lines.english: “Wh-what the hell are you doing, brat?! W-wait, not now! Let go of me!”

lines.japanese: 目の前で行われた一連の光景を、俺は呆然と見守ることしかできなかった。
lines.english: I could only stare blankly at the scene unfolding before me.

lines.japanese: はて、なんだろう。ツッコミどころは用意されてる気がするんだが、量が多すぎてどれから処理すればいいものやら。
lines.english: Hmm. I had the feeling that several obvious retorts were waiting, but there were too many to know which one to address first.

lines.japanese: 「ちょないない、これはねーって！　マジで！　羽田、見てねーでなんとかしろって！」
lines.english: “N-no, no, no! This can't be happening! Seriously! Haneda, quit staring and do something!”

lines.japanese: 「はっ、そうだった。マスターや他の男性客に見られないよう、俺が壁にならなければ！」
lines.english: “Ah! Of course. I must use my body as a wall so the boss and the other male customers can't see!”

lines.japanese: 「よし、ここは任せろ高内さん！　マスターは上の階へ上がったばかりだし、他の客は少ないし、俺が守ってみせる！」
lines.english: “Leave this to me, Takauchi! The boss just went upstairs, there are hardly any other customers, and I swear I'll protect you!”

lines.japanese: 「いいからこのガキ引っぺがしてよ！　私、手が使えねんだから！」
lines.english: “Just get this brat off me! Both my hands are tied up!”

lines.japanese: 「おねーちゃん、しましま穿かなそうなのにしましまなんだね」
lines.english: “Big sister, you don't look like you'd wear stripes, but yours are striped.”

lines.japanese: 「え、な、なにを……？」
lines.english: “Wh-what are you...?”

lines.japanese: 「わ～い、怖いおねえちゃんだけど、しましまだあー！」
lines.english: “Yay! You're scary, but you wear stripes!”

lines.japanese: 「うるっせえ！」
lines.english: “SHUT UP!”

lines.japanese: はっ。そういえばあまりの異常事態に見て見ぬふりをしたが、高内昌子がしましまパンツ？
lines.english: Wait. The situation was so bizarre that I had tried to ignore it, but Masako Takauchi wore striped panties?

lines.japanese: ひとの好み、それも女性の下着について言及する気はないが、意外といえば意外だなあ。
lines.english: I had no intention of commenting on another person's taste, especially in women's underwear, but it was unexpected.

lines.japanese: はっ。いやいや落ちついてる場合じゃないぞ。早く高内昌子を助けてあげなければ！
lines.english: Wait. This was no time for calm reflection! I had to help Masako Takauchi!

lines.japanese: 「真聡！」
lines.english: “Masato!”

lines.japanese: ん？　この子のお母さんか。
lines.english: Hm? Was that the child's mother?

lines.japanese: 「お母さん、ちょうどいいところに……一刻も早く助けてあげてください」
lines.english: “Ma'am, perfect timing... Please help her as quickly as possible.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、ごめんなさい、迷惑をかけて……真聡！　何してるの！？」
lines.english: “I'm so sorry he's bothering you... Masato! What do you think you're doing?!”

lines.japanese: 「ああいえ、真聡君？　ではなく」
lines.english: “No, not Masato. I mean—”

lines.japanese: 止めるべきなのは――と言おうとしたときには、母親は手を振りあげていた。
lines.english: I was about to tell her who actually needed stopping when the mother raised her hand.

lines.japanese: 「おかーさん、だってこのおねーちゃんしましまなんだよ」
lines.english: “But Mom, this big sister's panties are striped!”

lines.japanese: 「そんなこと言い訳になるはずないでしょう！」
lines.english: “That is no excuse!”

lines.japanese: 「ぎゃあああーっ！」
lines.english: “GYAAAAH!”

lines.japanese: 母親の一撃を脳天に喰らい、思わず手を離した真聡少年。だが、彼が地獄を見るのはこれからに違いない。
lines.english: The blow to the top of his head made young Masato release his grip. His time in hell, however, had surely only begun.

lines.japanese: ああ、高内昌子が少年を睨んでいる。子供には優しい俺だが、今回ばかりは他人ヅラを決めこませてもら――
lines.english: Masako Takauchi was glaring at the boy. I was gentle with children, but just this once, I would pretend this had nothing to do with me—

lines.japanese: 「羽田、オメなにひとのこと放置して見てんだよ」
lines.english: “Haneda, what the fuck are you doing just standing there watching me?”

lines.japanese: ――あれっ？　他人事じゃない？
lines.english: —huh? It did have something to do with me?

lines.japanese: 「い、いや、咄嗟に後ろ向いたからなにも見てないよ？」
lines.english: “I-I turned around immediately, so I didn't see anything!”

lines.japanese: 俺は大袈裟なほどぶんがぶんがと首を左右に動かした。
lines.english: I shook my head left and right with extravagant force.

lines.japanese: 「あ？　見てない？　マジで？」
lines.english: “What? You didn't see? Seriously?”

lines.japanese: 「う、うん」
lines.english: “R-right.”

lines.japanese: 「ふーん……あっそ」
lines.english: “Huh... Whatever.”

lines.japanese: あ、あれ？　怒ってはない？
lines.english: W-wait. She wasn't angry?

lines.japanese: センザンコウのように身を縮みこませる俺を無視して、センザンコウは自分の鞄を肩へ掛けた。
lines.english: Ignoring me as I curled up like a pangolin, the other pangolin slung her bag over her shoulder.

lines.japanese: 「悪い、なんか今ので疲れたから、もー帰るわ」
lines.english: “Sorry. That wore me out, so I'm going home.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ああ。また明日、学校でな」
lines.english: “O-okay. See you at school tomorrow.”

lines.japanese: な、なんか怒ってる？　でもそうじゃないのか？　あれ、よく分からないぞ？
lines.english: W-was she angry? Or wasn't she? I couldn't tell.

lines.japanese: 俺が悩んでるうちに、高内昌子は俺に背中を見せてしまっていた。
lines.english: While I agonized over it, Masako Takauchi turned her back on me.

lines.japanese: うーん、フォローの言葉だけは入れておいた方がいいんだろうか……彼女はひどい目にあって、傷付いてるのかもしれないからな。
lines.english: Hmm. Perhaps I should at least offer some words of comfort... She had suffered a terrible ordeal and might be hurt.

lines.japanese: ふむ、そういうことなら。俺はさっきまでの会話から、彼女の喜びそうな言葉をチョイスしてみた。
lines.english: Very well, then. Drawing on our earlier conversation, I selected the words most likely to please her.

lines.japanese: 「高内さん、さっきのはちょっと萌えキャラっぽかったぞ」
lines.english: “Takauchi, that was a little heart-melting.”

lines.japanese: 声が届いたのか、高内昌子の動きが止まった。
lines.english: Perhaps my voice reached her, because Masako Takauchi stopped.

lines.japanese: そして振りかえったときには鬼がいた。
lines.english: When she turned around, I saw a demon.

lines.japanese: ええっ、なんで怒ってんの！？　俺、言っちゃいけないこと言った？　もしかして？
lines.english: What?! Why was she angry? Did I say something I shouldn't have?

lines.japanese: 彼女はその表情のまましばらく唸り、そして沈黙を割くように、ふうとため息をついた。
lines.english: She growled with that expression for a while, then broke the silence with a long sigh.

lines.japanese: 「つかムカつくんだよ」
lines.english: “It just pisses me off.”

lines.japanese: 「そ、そうか、それはすまなかった」
lines.english: “I-I see. I'm sorry.”

lines.japanese: 「違げーよ、羽田じゃねーよ」
lines.english: “Not you, Haneda.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃ、じゃあ今の子供？」
lines.english: “Th-then the child?”

lines.japanese: 「……も、なんでもいーよ」
lines.english: “...Whatever. Who cares?”

lines.japanese: 最後に呟くように言葉を残して、高内昌子は帰っていった。
lines.english: Leaving those final muttered words behind, Masako Takauchi went home.

lines.japanese: なんだったんだ……？
lines.english: What had that been about...?
